title: US Retail Forex Deposits Fall to $462 Million, the Lowest Since at Least 2023
summary:
Customer deposits at US retail forex brokers fell to $462.31 million in June, a third straight monthly decline. The total is the lowest since at least September 2023, according to Commodity Futures Trading Commission filings.
Three months of losses have taken $26.29 million out of the industry since...
content:
2026-08-11T13:45:00.000+02:00

Tuesday, 11/08/2026 | 11:45 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • A third consecutive monthly decline wiped out the first-quarter recovery and undercut January's trough.
  • The regulator's figure moves with trading profit and loss as well as with client withdrawals.

Customer deposits at US retail forex brokers fell to $462.31 million in June, a third straight monthly decline. The total is the lowest since at least September 2023, according to Commodity Futures Trading Commission filings.

Three months of losses have taken $26.29 million out of the industry since March, a fall of 5.38% that erased the first-quarter recovery FinanceMagnates.com reported in May.

The industry has also dropped under the level that drew attention in January. That month's $472.96 million was the lowest in more than two years when FinanceMagnates.com first reported it. June closed $10.65 million below it.

OANDA and Charles Schwab Set Fresh Lows

OANDA ended June with $132.89 million, down 2.10% on the month. That is the smallest balance it has recorded in the data, and 3.62% less than it held a year earlier.

Charles Schwab's forex unit fell for a third month running, to $54.09 million. That figure is also a low for the series, and 12.91% below where the unit stood in June 2025.

Gain Capital, the StoneX subsidiary behind Forex .com, held $197.09 million and 42.6% of all US retail forex deposits. Its balance is the lowest since October 2023.

Those three hold 83.08% of the market between them, down 1.11 percentage points from a year ago. Every one of the six brokers ended June with less client money than it held in March.

A Year of Ownership Change at OANDA

OANDA has been through a change of owner and of management since FTMO bought it from CVC. The prop firm's founders took over as co-chief executives in March.

OANDA began moving its proprietary trading clients onto FTMO's platform on 2 March.

In Japan, OANDA more than doubled MetaTrader 4 margin requirements from 12 June, pushing accounts that could not meet them onto MetaTrader 5.

Neither change touches the US entity that files the CFTC numbers. OANDA has published no explanation for the fall in its American balances.

tastyfx and Trading.com Keep Their Annual Gains

tastyfx held $47.98 million, 1.92% lower on the month but 23.86% above June 2025. IG Group's US brand has added $9.24 million of client money in a year, after launching Prime accounts that paid up to 6% on idle cash last September.

Trading.com, the smallest of the six at 0.6% of deposits, was the only riser in June. The Trading Point subsidiary held $2.92 million, up 2.08% on May and 24.67% on a year earlier.

Between them the two hold $50.90 million, against $41.08 million in June 2025. The other four are all below where they were a year ago.

Interactive Brokers Shrinks in Forex While Its Brokerage Grows

Interactive Brokers reported $27.33 million, up 0.55% on the month after an 8.72% fall in May. Its forex balances are 21.31% below June 2025, the steepest annual drop of the six.

The wider brokerage went the other way. Interactive Brokers reported 5.26 million daily average revenue trades in June, 53% more than a year earlier, with client accounts up 34% to 5.18 million.

Client equity finished the month at $930.3 billion. Against that, the US retail forex book is a rounding error.

Its forex deposits have swung all year. They fell 20% in November before rebounding the following month.

What the CFTC Number Counts

Only six firms are registered to take retail forex deposits in the US. Dealers must hold at least $20 million in adjusted net capital, plus 5% of any retail forex obligation above $10 million.

The reported figure is a month-end snapshot of what those firms owe retail forex customers, and the CFTC adjusts it for realized and unrealized trading profit and loss.

A decline can therefore reflect customer withdrawals, trading losses, or both. The filings do not separate them.

title: TRON’s USDT Hits $87.9B as Q2 Transfers Reach $2.1T and Fees Jump 15.9%
summary:
Key Takeaways: The total stablecoin supply on TRON hit a new high of $89.2B, spearheaded by USDT. The network facilitated USDT transacting totaling $2.1T in Q2. TRX Supply continued to
The post TRON’s USDT Hits $87.9B as Q2 Transfers Reach $2.1T and Fees Jump 15.9% appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The total stablecoin supply on TRON hit a new high of $89.2B, spearheaded by USDT.
  • The network facilitated USDT transacting totaling $2.1T in Q2.
  • TRX Supply continued to be inflationary, and fees grew by 15.9%, to $699.4M.

TRON continued its impressive momentum, reaching new records for settlement and network activity during the quarter. In addition to less DeFi and DeX activity, Messari’s State of TRON Q2 2026 report revealed greater institutional access.

  • USDT Dominates TRON’s Stablecoin Market
  • Network Activity Sets Another Record
    • Fees Finally Reverse Their Decline
  • Institutional Access Expands
    • DeFi Activity Slips

USDT Dominates TRON’s Stablecoin Market

The cap of TRON’s stablecoins increased 4.1% QoQ to end Q2 at $89.2 billion. Stabilized token USDT was still overwhelmingly preferred as 98.5% of the network’s stablecoins are still in its hands.

Circulating USDT reached $87.9 billion, making TRON the largest USDT host chain ahead of Ethereum at $78.7 billion and BNB Chain at $9.2 billion.

The activity of USDT also increased. During Q2, TRON processed $2.1 trillion in USDT transactions and the average daily transaction volume rose 4.3% to $22.8 billion. On 20th May, the USDT’s supply peaked at an all-time high of $89 billion.

The figure points to TRON remaining a significant network for USDT transactions, especially for those looking for moderately priced transfers.

Read More: TRON Hits $167B Stablecoin Volume as Daily Transactions Surge Past 10.6M

Network Activity Sets Another Record

TRON’s broader usage also reached new highs. Average daily transactions were up 8.7% QoQ to 11.8, totaling approximately 1.08 billion transactions in all, in the quarter. The network has already recorded a record 14.6 million transaction flow on 15 June.

The average daily active addresses increased by 11.7% to 3.6 million, a 4.5% increase after a significant drop in Q1.

Fees Finally Reverse Their Decline

Higher activity helped TRON’s fee market recover after several quarters of pressure.

The total network fees rose by 15.9% QoQ to USD 699.4 million, the first quarterly rise since the fee reduction in August 2025. Fees also rose 2.1% in TRX terms to 2.10 billion TRX.

The average transaction cost was $0.65, or 5.4% higher. But more usage did not mean more deflationary value of TRX. Circulating supply rose by 87 million TRX or 0.1%, making it the third quarter of the third inflationary trend.

Read More: TRON Raises $26M in 30 Days to Top Blockchain Revenue Rankings

Institutional Access Expands

In addition, a number of events regarding regulated financial products and trading venues occurred in TRON.

Securitize launched its Hamilton Lane tokenized Senior Credit Opportunities Fund on TRON in June, launching the first Securitized asset on the TRON network. The fund began with just about $4.3 million in assets under management.

TRX has also secured more market access avenues with Bitnomial, adding spot TRX trading, and OKX Europe, introducing MiFID-regulated TRX expiry perpetuals. Binance.US re-instated TRX trading and Grayscale added TRX to its list of assets under consideration for the Q2.

DeFi Activity Slips

Not all metrics improved. TRON’s DeFi TVL declined 1.9% to $4.4 billion, while average daily DEX volume fell 21.7% to $49.3 million, marking a fourth consecutive quarterly decline.

JustLend remained the largest DeFi protocol, although its TVL dropped 10.5% to $2.9 billion. USDD moved in the opposite direction, with TVL rising 25.5% to $1.2 billion.

Alongside the stablecoin growth of their stable products, TRON also expanded its infrastructure by launching post-quantum signature technology on their testnet Nile and developed its $1 billion AI Fund strategy.

title: Meta’s Bet: Personal AI for Billions, Not Institutions
summary: Mark Zuckerberg is committing $135B to a radically different AI strategy, one that positions Meta as the distributor of superintelligence to individuals, not enterprises.
content:
Skip to content

Mark Zuckerberg is committing $135B to a radically different AI strategy, one that positions Meta as the distributor of superintelligence to individuals, not enterprises.

Mark Zuckerberg published his case for personal superintelligence on Monday and, the same morning, shipped the thing that makes the case affordable.

In The Future is for Everyone, dated 10 August, he reaches for a comparison this publication is named for: the towns that brought railroads, highways, electrification and broadband became centres of research, business and industry, and he argues AI infrastructure can do the same for the places that host it. The promise on offer is an agent that works “24/7 on your behalf” across health, career, finances, home and hobbies, free for billions of people, with heavier users priced by what he calls a “dynamic auction mechanism.”

I believe everyone should have access to superintelligence, and I wrote a long piece about Meta’s philosophy and values for building a positive future for everyone. https://t.co/2ZoNZXZ39T

— Mark Zuckerberg (@finkd) August 10, 2026

Hours before it went up, Meta Superintelligence Labs published Muse Glimmer: a 30-billion-parameter agentic model, weights released under a permissive Apache 2.0 licence, small enough to run on a Mac or PC with a single consumer GPU. That is the manifesto’s economics, shipped as a checkpoint rather than a pledge.

What personal superintelligence looks like when it works

Zuckerberg’s examples are domestic and present-tense. His agent flags information and helps him prototype; it monitors his sleep, then watches him train and gives feedback; it plans personalised recipes for him and his daughter to bake each weekend and orders the ingredients. His eight-year-old codes her own ideas and produces videos in an evening, and the two of them are designing a robot together. Meta researchers, he writes, are generating novel crystal structures suited to augmented-reality glasses.

Follow that line forward and the claims get larger. A tutor with a PhD in every subject, giving the help that currently goes only to students whose parents can pay for it. Biohub’s open-source virtual-cell and protein models already in the hands of researchers designing drugs, against a goal Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan set of curing or preventing all disease this century, which he says he now expects sooner. Occupations that barely exist yet: one-person studios designing custom furniture and clothing, world builders, personal biologists formulating individual treatments. These are his projections, and they are labelled as such throughout the document. They are also the clearest statement yet of what the capex is for.

Why cost per user decides Meta’s bet

A persistent agent for a billion people is a different inference problem from an enterprise API. Enterprise pricing recovers cost per call. A free agent running continuously does not, and the promise of round-the-clock service commits Meta to standing capacity at a scale it has to pay for before anyone pays it back.

The balance sheet shows the scale of the commitment. Meta narrowed its 2026 capital-expenditure guidance to $130–145bn on 29 July, from a prior range of $125–145bn, and recorded $31.08bn of capex in the second quarter alone. Full-year 2025 capex was $72.22bn. Free cash flow for the quarter came in at $784m, against $8.55bn a year earlier.

Muse Glimmer is the first concrete answer to that arithmetic, and it points away from the data centre. At full precision a 30-billion-parameter model needs over 55GB of memory; Meta compressed the weights to roughly 4-bit precision, bringing the language model under 20GB and leaving headroom for the KV cache, the image-understanding encoder and a speculative-decoding drafter inside a 24GB or 32GB envelope. Meta says the compression cost minimal to no degradation on agentic tasks. On its own published comparison, Glimmer leads Gemma4-31B and Qwen3.6-27B on MCP Atlas at 75.5 against 54.2 and 62.5, and scores 51.2 on SWE-Bench Pro, while trailing Qwen on computer-use and terminal work. Meta’s benchmarks, on Meta’s chart, awaiting third-party runs.

Locally. That is the load-bearing word. A model built for always-on local workflows that keeps working with or without a network connection is an agent whose marginal token Meta never pays to serve. Zuckerberg has said weights for Muse Spark 2.1 follow in the coming weeks, which suggests this is the direction rather than a one-off.

What the dynamic auction still has to prove

The manifesto’s pricing claim is that the auction will guarantee everyone the lowest possible price for the intelligence and compute they use, while directing capacity towards whatever people collectively find most valuable. That is a stronger claim than a rationing mechanism, and it arrives without a unit, a reserve price or any description of how the market clears. Publishing those mechanics is the single most useful thing Meta could do next, because it is where an affordability promise either becomes a number or stays a sentence.

Two other commitments are worth holding Meta to, and both are cheap to verify later. The first is governance: Meta says it is giving its independent board of directors the power to approve the safety criteria for model releases and to review whether each release meets them, and encourages other labs to adopt the same structure. The second is the community compact behind the buildout, of which Zuckerberg’s own example is Richland Parish, Louisiana, where he says teachers received a $50,000 bonus this year from the tax revenue of a Meta data centre — funded through a $1bn fund directed at the US communities hosting its facilities. Meta also commits to restoring more water than it uses in its watersheds by 2030, and 200% of it in areas of high water stress. Those are checkable in twelve months. Checking them is how the compact becomes a standard instead of a paragraph.

The tracks being laid here run from the data centre to the desk, and now to the phone. On 10 August a model capable of planning, calling tools and recovering from its own failures became something you can download and run on hardware you already own. The weights are on Hugging Face. Whatever the auction eventually charges for the compute that will not fit on a laptop, the version that does fit is already free, and the next one is a few weeks out.

title: Blockstream Debuts Swaps, Allowing Bitcoiners to Move Between Lightning and Main Network With Ease
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Blockstream Debuts Swaps, Allowing Bitcoiners to Move Between Lightning and Main Network With Ease 
Following the suspension of Boltz, Blocksteam is debuting a feature allowing trustless Bitcoin swaps. 
This post Blockstream Debuts Swaps, Allowing Bitcoiners to Move Between Lightni...
content:
Bitcoin infrastructure company Blockstream has announced a new feature allowing users to make trustless swaps. 

Dubbed Blockstream Swaps, the idea is that Bitcoiners will be able to quickly move between the main chain and Lightning network. 

It comes after non-custodial Bitcoin swap provider Boltz suspended its service after it said attackers were finding vulnerabilities faster than its team could fix using AI. 

“In support of the broader Bitcoin and Liquid ecosystem, Blockstream is launching Blockstream Swaps,” Blockstream said. 

“This initiative was already under development to ensure a resilient suite of utility for the ecosystem, and it complements the providers already doing this work rather than replacing any one of them.”

The idea, added Blockstream, is users can move funds across layers while never losing full control over their funds.

To use Lightning, users will not need to run a node or channel — as is normally needed with Lightning — and can simply hold a Bitcoin or LBTC balance and let a swap convert at the moment of payment.

LBTC is the native asset of the Liquid Network, a Bitcoin layer-2 sidechain created by Blockstream. 

“This initiative was already under development to ensure a resilient suite of utility for the ecosystem, and it complements the providers already doing this work rather than replacing any one of them,” added Blocksteam’s announcement. 

Boltz this month suspended its Bitcoin swap service. It said that a surge in AI-assisted attacks left it unable to continue operating safely.

Crypto hacks have surged, with security experts warning that cybercriminals are using AI to search for bugs in crypto projects and then take advantage of errors auditors may have missed.

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: North Korean Hackers Deploy 3 Local AI Systems to Supercharge Crypto Attacks
summary:
Key Takeaways: Kimsuky was using Ollama, GPT4All and Msty, three local LLM environments. Crypto, financial and investment targets are being scammed using AI-generated documents. The group remains using LNK files,
The post North Korean Hackers Deploy 3 Local AI Systems to Supercharge Crypto Attacks a...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Kimsuky was using Ollama, GPT4All and Msty, three local LLM environments.
  • Crypto, financial and investment targets are being scammed using AI-generated documents.
  • The group remains using LNK files, and PowerShell and GitHub based infrastructure.

North Korea-linked hacking group Kimsuky is moving deeper into artificial intelligence, with new research showing the attackers are building local AI environments and using generative tools in campaigns targeting cryptocurrency and financial-sector users.

South Korean cybersecurity firm Genians said the activity is part of Kimsuky’s broader attack operations rather than a standalone campaign. The researchers track the activity as Operation GitPower, which builds on tactics previously associated with the FlowerPower campaign.

  • Kimsuky Builds Local AI Infrastructure
  • AI-Generated Documents Target Crypto Users
    • Polished Lures Replace Crude Phishing
    • Crypto Targets Remain in the Crosshairs

Kimsuky Builds Local AI Infrastructure

Genians found that Ollama, GPT4All and Msty were tools used to run Kimsuky local LLM environments. The group was also seen exploring technologies such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and the AI coding assistant Cursor.

The results indicate that Kimsuky does not rely on public AI chatbots just for occasional tasks. Rather, the community seems to be gearing up for integrating AI into various segments of the attack process.

By running AI models locally, attackers can also gain more control over the data and operations they use. Sensitive questions, program development and information collected can be analyzed without strict dependence on third-party cloud AI services.

Genians stated that evidence suggests it is an era of developing capabilities, in which AI may be used to aid in the creation of malware, information analysis as well as information automation in attacks.

Read More: $290M KelpDAO Hack SHOCK: LayerZero Points to Fatal DVN Flaw, Lazarus Suspected

AI-Generated Documents Target Crypto Users

Polished Lures Replace Crude Phishing

The most obvious shift is that of Kimsuky’s phishing materials.

Genians discovered content logs regarding virtual assets, financial investment, and game development with indications of content generation involving AI. The documents were professionally organized, in natural language, very similar to real business letters.

Researchers also found metadata is associated with certain English-language documents that link them to python-docx or WPS Office, and the documents’ creation and modification dates had surprisingly regular patterns. The results were evaluated for its implication of an automated document production process.

In yet another campaign, a malicious LNK file was disguised as an investment strategy document. The lure was similar to a Korean fintech site, making it more likely that potential victims would believe what was being sent.

Crypto Targets Remain in the Crosshairs

Kimsuky continues to attack organisations and professionals related to virtual assets, finance, diplomacy, security and international affairs.

The technical delivery chain remains familiar. The victim then gets the malicious LNK shortcuts packaged as valid archives and in ZIP format. When run, the files can unhide any command-line instructions or PowerShell loaders.

Defenders were advised to stay vigilant for any unusual execution arguments to the LNK, PowerShell arguments hidden in files, scheduled tasks, access to GitHub Raw Contents API, use of unusual personal access tokens, or .data (encrypted) arguments.

title: Australia Shuts Down 96 Crypto ATMs After Cryptolink Faces AML Reporting Crackdown
summary:
Key Takeaways: AUSTRAC has imposed a three-month ban on Cryptolink’s VASP registration. All of the company’s 96 crypto ATMs have to be removed from service in Australia. A lack of
The post Australia Shuts Down 96 Crypto ATMs After Cryptolink Faces AML Reporting Crackdown appeared first on CryptoNinj...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • AUSTRAC has imposed a three-month ban on Cryptolink’s VASP registration.
  • All of the company’s 96 crypto ATMs have to be removed from service in Australia.
  • A lack of reports on transactions along with concerns of high-risk use of cryptocurrencies were cited as regulatory reasons.

Australia’s financial crime regulator has withheld its license because the operator of Cryptolink’s cryptocurrency ATMs has failed to fully resolve issues with money laundering controls. Following suspension on August 9, this will leave 96 machines off-line for three months.

  • AUSTRAC Suspends Cryptolink’s Crypto ATM Operations
    • Previous $56,340 Penalty Failed to Resolve Concerns
  • Crypto ATMs Face Closer Regulatory Scrutiny

AUSTRAC Suspends Cryptolink’s Crypto ATM Operations

Registration of the company as a Virtual Asset Service Provider (VASP) has been suspended by the Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre (AUSTRAC), which will not allow the company to run its cryptocurrency Automatic Teller Machines (CATM).

Cryptolink is able to provide the machines that enable customers to trade cash for cryptocurrency. The body AUSTRAC cautioned that the firm would continue to be vigilant in detecting and regulating transactions that may be linked to money launderers or terrorists.

AUSTRAC Chief Executive Brendan Thomas said that the regulator had provided Cryptolink with sufficient time to rectify its compliance issues, but the company was then unable to keep up with some basic reporting requirements.

The main problem had to do with threshold transaction reports which form part of Australia’s AML/CTF regime. AUSTRAC found that Cryptolink failed to provide reports and did not get back to the regulator regarding requests for information.

Read More: 190 Million in Crypto Washed: Australia Cuts Off Sophisticated Money Laundering Ring

Previous $56,340 Penalty Failed to Resolve Concerns

This new suspension is the continuation of a process started last year by the administration. In October 2025, AUSTRAC accepted an enforceable undertaking from Cryptolink after its Cryptocurrency Taskforce identified alleged breaches of AML laws. Those concerns were reflected in the lack of timely reporting of threshold transactions and inadequacies in the firm’s AML/CTF risk assessments.

Cryptolink also was notified and fined $56,340 for infringing. However the company, though it fulfilled the terms of that commitment, subsequently failed to uphold these reporting requirements, AUSTRAC said. The regulator thus decided that Cryptolink was too risky to continue running.

Crypto ATMs Face Closer Regulatory Scrutiny

The development follows a trend of regulatory scrutiny over cryptocurrency ATMs to facilitate exchanges between cash and digital currencies, unlike traditional cryptocurrency exchanges.

The regulator has set up its Crypto Taskforce and has since undertaken supervisory engagements with crypto ATM providers since the end of 2024. AUSTRAC has also identified that the use of digital currency would be a potential area to closely monitor as being able to be used to facilitate the movement of funds rapidly and across borders.

Thomas stated that, while Cryptolink is suspended, AUSTRAC will keep an eye on the company to ensure it complies with the order. The regulator also cautioned that it will also persist in its efforts with cryptocurrency enterprises with respect to serious AML/CTF risk and compliance breaches.

With a suspension period of three months, the 96 CATM’s that Cryptolink is processing are unable to function during that three-month interval. Until the company has resolved AUSTRAC’s concerns, it will be unable to re-enter the Australian crypto ATM market.

Immediate attention is on crypto access for now. Superhero Crypto provides the Australian investor with a familiar and user-friendly platform for purchasing and holding digital assets, while Bitstamp by Robinhood provides the infrastructure.

title: XRP Ledger Foundation Warning as Fake Rewards and Wallet Phishing Surge Online
summary:
Key Takeaways: The XRP Ledger Foundation stated that there are no XRP airdrops, rewards, or wallet scanning programs. RippleX uncovered fake “XRP Rewards Scanner” scams that hijack wallets using phishing
The post XRP Ledger Foundation Warning as Fake Rewards and Wallet Phishing Surge Online appeared...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The XRP Ledger Foundation stated that there are no XRP airdrops, rewards, or wallet scanning programs.
  • RippleX uncovered fake “XRP Rewards Scanner” scams that hijack wallets using phishing attacks.
  • Ripple reminded users to check messages and posts via official channels and do not share private keys or recovery phrases.

Scammers are intensifying their phishing attack campaign targeting XRP owners with bogus reward offers and wallet validations respectively, prompting the XRP Ledger Foundation to give another warning. The warning comes at a time when crypto fraud is getting even more sophisticated, targeting trusted companies on social media platforms.

Security PSA: Phishing attempts and fake giveaway posts are becoming more common across 𝕏. Be careful with posts you’re tagged in and accounts impersonating people or organizations you trust.

Ripple is not running an “XRP Rewards Scanner” or offering unclaimed XRP through a…

— RippleX (@RippleXDev) August 6, 2026

  • Fake XRP Rewards Campaigns Target Community
    • Phishing Tactics Continue to Evolve
  • Ripple Shares Practical Security Advice
    • Community Asked to Report Fraud Quickly

Fake XRP Rewards Campaigns Target Community

The XRP Ledger Foundation stated that none of the XRP ecosystem, which includes the XRP Foundation and Ripple, are distributing free XRP or conducting reward campaigns or wallet scanning services.

It also cautioned users that the organisation will not reach out to them directly with a message asking them to connect their wallets or giving out wallet information. If there is a promotion offering free XRP and/or wallet information, then it’s suspicious.

RippleX, Ripple’s developer platform, echoed the warning after fraudulent posts began circulating on X promoting a fake “XRP Rewards Scanner.” The posts falsely claimed users could recover unclaimed XRP simply by scanning or connecting their wallets.

Read More: T54 Introduces New Agent Payments on XRP Ledger

Phishing Tactics Continue to Evolve

That’s repeatedly being done through fake promotional posts that try to look authentic by tagging legitimate users, according to RippleX. Another ploy involves a fabricated image of Ripple providing unclaimed XRP; this has also been disseminated.

RippleX strongly urged the users to double check all announcements on the official Ripple and XRP Ledger pages and not connect a wallet, endorse any transactions or engage in any new websites before using them.

Ripple Shares Practical Security Advice

Phishing, fake giveaways, impersonation accounts, deep-fake videos and malicious websites appear to be the most prevalent crypto scams tricking investors today, according to Ripple.

It is also advisable for users to use the most up-to-date web browsers equipped with robust support against phishing attacks and wallet software that filters transactions to suspicious addresses.

More to the point, Ripple again said that no legitimate organization will ever ask for a wallet’s secret key or recovery phrase.

Community Asked to Report Fraud Quickly

Users should report any phishing campaigns or impersonated accounts as soon as they occur, according to Ripple. The company also added that stolen assets in blockchain transactions are frequently hard to retrieve because of the decentralized nature of the XRP Ledger in which no single entity has the authority to cancel out assets transferred.

This new alert comes as the industry experiences widespread crypto scam surges.

Ripple and the XRP Ledger Foundation are trying to get people to pause and double-check each message, and to keep this one thing in mind: If it’s someone promising you “free XRP,” or asking you to provide the keys to your wallet, it’s likely a scam.

title: Wintermute Enters $60T Wall Street Arena With SEC License to Power Tokenized Securities Boom
summary:

content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Wintermute USA is now an SEC-registered broker-dealer and member of FINRA.
  • The approval will broaden its institutional trading capabilities in the U.S. market.
  • The move will bolster Wintermute’s foothold in the emerging tokenized securities marketplace.

After receiving permission from the Securities and Exchange Commission to play in the U.S. securities landscape, Wintermute has gone quite a distance in expanding the crypto-native trading category.

The milestone brings direct access to traditional financial infrastructure to one of the industry’s largest liquidity providers and enhances its long-term effort to connect and earmark portfolios of digital assets and traditional capital markets.

  • Wintermute Expands Into Regulated U.S. Markets
  • Digital Assets and Traditional Finance Continue to Converge
    • Building Infrastructure for Tokenized Securities
    • Institutional Expansion Gains Momentum

Wintermute Expands Into Regulated U.S. Markets

Wintermute has announced that its U.S. subsidiary, Wintermute USA LLC, is registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and has come on board to the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA).

Good morning, USA 🇺🇸

Wintermute USA is now an SEC-registered broker-dealer and FINRA member (https://t.co/7rQGL6UzX6)

The registration marks Wintermute’s entry into U.S. regulated markets and strengthens our coverage of institutional counterparties in the region pic.twitter.com/IBZBbAB7GP

— Wintermute (@wintermute_t) August 6, 2026

The registration makes Wintermute USA a regulated proprietary trading firm that can provide liquidity on the national securities exchanges and in the over-the-counter (OTC) markets in the U.S. and other jurisdictions.

It now can trade U.S. equities and equity options on its own behalf, or for itself as an Authorized Participant (AP) in transaction of securities as part of an exchange-traded product, including those that are crypto-trust or cryptolinked equity securities or equity-offices.

The approval will put Wintermute in a better position to service institutional counterparties in the U.S. and help the company grow toward the next wave in financial tokenization, the company said.

Read More: SEC Eyes Tokenized Stocks Plan That Could Unlock Trillions in Crypto Trading Markets

Digital Assets and Traditional Finance Continue to Converge

Wintermute founder and CEO Evgeny Gaevoy said the company has always expected digital assets and traditional finance to evolve together rather than compete.

Building Infrastructure for Tokenized Securities

Institutional adoption will grow, and those firms able to bridge the gap between the blockchain-money and traditional financial markets will fare best, Gaevoy said.

With the new status, Wintermute will be able to get more entrenched in securities trading, and feature gold with crypto-linked exchange-traded products. It also establishes a groundwork for further activities in the tokenized securities field, where regulators, asset managers, and exchanges are increasingly focused.

Institutional Expansion Gains Momentum

Wintermute’s current average trading volume is in excess of $10 billion per day and it offers liquidity on over 60 centralized and decentralized exchanges globally.

The business will be run by a dedicated team within the company in New York as it keeps building its relationship with U.S. institutions and regulators, the company’s New York arm said.

The Wall Street Journal also noted that the broker-dealer registration would also help Wintermute gain access to market-making functions on the major exchanges in the United States, like the Nasdaq National Security Marketplace and the New York Stock Exchange, which allow market makers to maintain market liquidity in specific securities.

The new licence should give Wintermute a whole new ability to take on battle with the old line electronic trading companies and bring its experience in liquidity to the regulated financial realm too.

What Are the Best Features of BingX?

The Best Features of BingX include Futures and Spot trading, Copy trading, Grid Trading Bots, Crypto Staking, and a P2P marketplace to help users complete transactions with one another. Now, let’s walk through the details of these features and how you can use them to maximize your crypto investment.

Spot and Futures Trading

In Spot markets, users can buy and sell cryptocurrencies for immediate delivery while enjoying profits or incurring losses directly from changes in the cryptocurrency value. On BingX, spot trading supports two types of orders: Market orders and Limit orders.

The first is a type of order in which you execute a buy or sell order immediately at the best price in the current market for fast trading. Meanwhile, Limit orders are a type of order where you can set the amount and the highest buy price or lowest sell price you can take.

When the market price matches your expectations, the system will automatically execute the order at the best price within the limit price range you set.

Here’s an example of how the two order types on BingX’s Spot Market work:

If you place a market order to buy ETH at the current market price, 3700 USDT. You can simply set the amount you want (e.g 100 USDT). The order will then be filled immediately when you initiate the transaction.

On the other hand, if you want to buy ETH at a lower price of 3500 USDT and the last price was 3700, you can choose the limit order and set the buy price at 3500 USDT. The limit order will be filled when the price of the coin drops to 3500 USDT. The same goes for selling crypto at a higher price than the current market price.

BingX also provides a Futures Trading Interface, which allows users to trade against the future price of a particular token while amplifying earnings through leverage.

For futures on BingX, you can either go long (buy) or short (sell) a trading pair to capitalize on the market price volatility. The trading platform provides two types of futures trading: Standard Futures and Perpetual Futures (USDT-M and Coin-M).

  1. Standard Futures Contracts

These contracts have a set expiration date on which a trader can agree to buy or sell a specific digital asset at a predetermined price. It is ideal for inexperienced traders; the trading interface is straightforward, intuitive, and easy to navigate.

Also, transactions on the Standard Futures Market are concluded quickly, making it perfect for investors who are currently on a tight budget.

  1. Perpetual Futures Contracts

Perpetual futures contracts do not have expiration dates, and you can hold them as long as you want to maximize your profits. BingX offers two margin modes in their perpetual futures market: USDT-margined (USDT-M) and Coin-margined (Coin-M). USDT-M.

That being said, the next question is, which one is best for you? Well, it depends on your experience and requirements, but here’s a guide on how to select between the Standard and Perpetual Futures trading on BingX.

Choose standard futures:

  • If you are new to futures.
  • If you need fast order execution.
  • If you prefer a more straightforward and faster trading process.
  • If you are interested in trading foreign currencies, international indices, and commodities.
  • If you would like to experiment with standard Coin-M futures.

Choose perpetual futures:

  • If you already have experience in trading futures.
  • If you invest large amounts of money in crypto.
  • If you need to trade without slippage when opening/closing positions.
  • If you need a more functional and sophisticated trading interface.
  • If you need greater market depth and higher liquidity.

Whichever one you decide on, BingX has an advanced slippage mechanism that initiates accurate stop losses to prevent you from losing a significant amount of money on trades.

Copy Trading

BingX has one of the best copy trading platforms where users can copy the strategies of more experienced traders to avoid losing your hard earned money. BingX copy trading has over 17,000 professional elite traders divided into categories, like trending traders and conservative traders.

Unlike other crypto exchanges that display minimal information on their Master Traders, BingX’s copy trading feature shows Copiers in-depth information to help them make suitable choices. Once you select an elite trader you want to copy, any trade they make is automatically replicated in your account. You also don’t have to worry about losses because BingX offers a Copy Trading Subsidy Voucher to safeguard your trades. Grid Trading Bots

BingX’s Grid Trading Bots can automatically buy crypto low and sell high 24/7, according to previously set instructions. These bots are designed to yield returns from market volatility, and they can operate 24/7, eliminating the need for you to constantly monitor your trades.

BingX offers three Grid Trading Bots for different markets, and they include the Futures Grid (amplifying margins and profits), Spots Grid (quick buy and sell), and the Spot Infinity Grid (advanced spot grid).

The Spot Infinity Grid is also known as “Never-Exit-Trades-Early Grid.” Unlike Spot Grid, the Spot Infinity Grid does not require you to set an upper price limit. This helps avoid a common issue in Spot Grid when the price exceeds the upper limit, resulting in missed opportunities.

Spot Infinity Grid, on the other hand, allows users to hold onto their digital assets in a rising market. So, whether you are active or not, and as long as the market fluctuates up or down, you will make more profit than you probably would using the regular Spot Grid.

BingX Wealth

BingX Wealth is an all-in-one asset management service where users earn interest and achieve stable returns on their funds or crypto they are not using at that moment. This feature supports mainstream cryptocurrencies such as USDT, BTC, ETH, XRP, and more.

BingX Wealth offers two main modes of earnings to cater to different users: Flexible Term and Fixed-term. Whether you decide to use the flexible or fixed-term option, here are the benefits of opting for the BingX Wealth program:

  • Zero Fees: No fees are charged for subscription and redemption.
  • Steady and Reliable: BingX has passed the Merkle Tree Proof of Reserves (POR) verification. Proving that they provide 100% asset collateralization and ensure the security of users’ assets.

Additionally, the platform has a thorough risk control system, robust security measures, and advanced infrastructure used to safeguard all user assets.

  • Taker Fee: You pay this fee when you remove liquidity by placing an order that matches an existing order. These fees are higher and are filled immediately.

The post US Treasury Sanctions 2 Iran-Linked Crypto Exchanges in $5M Money-Laundering Case a...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Shelbit, Aban Tether, and Siavash Kayvanpour, a cryptocurrency operator, were sanctioned by OFAC.
  • The U.S. authorities accused the network of assisting in the evasion of sanctions and linkages to the IRGC.
  • The action blocks U.S.-related property and transactions with designated entities.

The U.S. Treasury Department has heightened its pressure on Iranian crypto networks accusing exchanges and companies of helping to launder shady digital funds. The new move adds a new strain on crypto platforms that conduct business in and with Iran’s financial sector.

  • Treasury Targets Iran-Linked Crypto Network
  • Aban Tether Also Added to the Sanctions List
    • Crypto Exchanges Face Growing Sanctions Risks

Treasury Targets Iran-Linked Crypto Network

The Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced sanctions on August 7 against two digital asset exchanges, Shelbit and Aban Tether, along with Siavash Kayvanpour, whom authorities identified as a key figure behind a network of companies involved in illicit crypto activity.

The network enabled the transfer and anonymisation of digital assets linked to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and played a role in sanctions-evasion activities, Treasury said.

In total, IRGC controlled crypto addresses sent over $1 million to wallets associated with Shelbit, the agency said. In total, over $2 million was sent from addresses associated with Shelbit to wallets in the hands of the IRGC.

Kayvanpour addresses also wired over $2 million in crypto to Nobitex, an Iranian exchange that prior to this incident was banned by the U.S. government.

The Treasury also claimed that Shelbit processed tens of millions of dollars in digital assets linked to an online gambling website in Persian. Those flows were used to mask the source of the money, the agency said.

Read More: Iran Shock Sends Oil to Hyperliquid as 24/7 Crypto Markets Steal Spotlight

Aban Tether Also Added to the Sanctions List

OFAC also separately designated Iran-based digital currency exchange Aban Tether. The platform has reportedly conducted millions of dollars worth of transactions with such previously sanctioned Iranian exchanges as Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin and Ramzinex.

It was designated in Executive Order 13902, which empowers the U.S. government to impose designations on companies that operate in Iran’s financial sector.

Crypto Exchanges Face Growing Sanctions Risks

In the case of the sanctions, property and interests in property of any of the designated entities and interests controlled by U.S. persons are blocked. Band trading in those assets will normally not be allowed without an OFAC authorization or exemption.

The restrictions can also extend to entities owned 50% or more, directly or indirectly, by blocked persons.

The Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the department already is working to disrupt illegal financial networks, whether they are tied to traditional currencies or cryptocurrencies.

The action was linked to the IRS Criminal Investigation, and the State Department’s Rewards for Justice program has been promising up to $15 Million for information that can disrupt the IRGC’s financial mechanisms.

The decision underlines the critical role that sanctions screening, wallet surveillance, and transaction checks will play in crypto businesses and exchanges engaging with entities linked to high-risk countries.
